extracted.intended_audience: aspiring prestidigitators, stage performers, and theatrical directors interested in 19th-century performance practice and audience management
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and rhetorical principles for performing prestidigitation/ventriloquy and for managing theatrical presentations and audiences, drawn from a 19th-century practitioner's memoir. Covers audience psychology, presentation style, advertising/ticketing tactics, and safety cautions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age appropriateness for prestidigitation
rubrics_metrics.description: «Le public accordera bien à un homme de trente-cinq à quarante ans le droit de le tromper et de lui faire subir ces amusantes déceptions; il ne l'accordera pas à un jeune homme.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A performer should consider apparent age and gravitas: audiences more readily accept deception from performers whose age implies experience and study. Young performers risk being judged implausible in roles requiring assumed expertise; adapt repertoire/character accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study the spectator as much as the act
rubrics_metrics.description: «n’ayant pas à me préoccuper des expériences, j’étudiais autant le spectateur que le physicien lui-même.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe and learn from audience reactions and remarks. Audience study informs choice of effects, patter, and pacing; valuable insights often come from ordinary spectators' observations rather than specialist sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: It is more difficult to fool an ignorant person than a man of wit
rubrics_metrics.description: «L’homme vulgaire... Pour lui, les séances de prestidigitation deviennent un combat dont il veut à tout prix sortir vainqueur... toujours en garde contre les paroles dorées... mes yeux ne quitteront pas ses mains... Il s’ensuit que l’escamoteur... doit redoubler d’adresse.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor methods to audience type: so-called 'vulgar' or suspicious spectators scrutinize hands and resist rhetorical misdirection, demanding greater manual dexterity and subtler misdirection. Conversely, cultivated spectators often abandon scepticism and willingly engage in illusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer astonishment over laughter
rubrics_metrics.description: «Mieux vaut l’étonnement cent fois que le fou rire.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for wonder and lasting surprise rather than cheap laughs. Laughter ('fou rire') is ephemeral and leaves no memory of the effect; design acts to produce astonishment that will be remembered and talked about.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid calembours and excessive verbal compliments in modern taste
rubrics_metrics.description: «Le calembour n’a plus la même faveur... Le langage symbolique, complimenteur et parfumé, est aussi complètement tombé en désuétude...»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Witty puns and ornate complimentary patter can provoke laughter that undermines the effect and may seem pretentious. Modern audiences (in the author's time) prefer direct astonishment; adapt verbal style to contemporary tastes and avoid overused wordplay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate treatment of ladies and gentlemen in performance
rubrics_metrics.description: «la base fondamentale des séances de Comte était les mystifications aux Messieurs (les souverains exceptés), les compliments aux Dames et les calembours à tout le monde.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use social conventions strategically: flatter and present gracious effects for female spectators, employ teasing mystifications for men (within safety and decorum), but avoid exposing individuals to embarrassment. Tailor interactions by gender expectations of the audience and locale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ventriloquism as both theatrical device and publicity tool
rubrics_metrics.description: La ventriloquie... permettre d'imiter la voix humaine et de la combiner avec intelligence... il jette la terreur dans une diligence... il remet à chacun l’offrande qu’il a faite à la peur...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ventriloquism can create on-stage interludes, off-stage mystifications, and publicity stunts. Employed cleverly it attracts crowds and can be used to stage surprizes in public spaces, but requires caution as off-stage mystifications can be misinterpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ clever promotional and box-office tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemples de procédés de Comte: «les billets de famille», «les médailles», «les loges réservées aux lauréats des pensions et des collèges», et l'usage d'un café attenant comme bureau de location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directors can increase receipts by creative ticketing (discounted family tickets), perceived exclusivity (reserved boxes), small paid souvenirs (medals) and by leveraging adjacent businesses to ease access. Such measures change audience composition and can boost revenue—but be transparent about value to avoid alienation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not publicly embarrass spectators (especially ladies)
rubrics_metrics.description: «les dames qui assistent à une séance de prestidigitation, y viennent pour se récréer l’esprit et non pour être elles-mêmes mises en scène... elles préfèrent rester simples spectatrices plutôt que de se voir exposées...»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid making audience members the butt of jokes or putting them on display in ways that humiliate. Maintain respect and ensure that participant-focused effects feel like honorific gestures rather than public exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt to the tastes of the age and locality; multiple genres can succeed
rubrics_metrics.description: «Comte agissait avec le sien; tous deux nous avons réussi avec des principes différents; ce qui prouve que: 'Tous les genres sont bons, hors le genre ennuyeux.'»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different performance styles work in different contexts. Successful performers adapt to their epoch's tastes and local audiences. The only true failure is boring the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public mystifications can provoke dangerous reactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Anecdotes: Comte faillit être frappé par des paysans fanatiques en Suisse; on le prit pour un sorcier et l'assaillit à coups de bâtons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious with public stunts that might be interpreted as sorcery or deceptive coercion, especially in rural or superstitious contexts. Consider local beliefs and safety; publicity that humiliates or frightens people can have violent consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misdirection requires matching rhetorical patter and manual skill
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations about the ignorant focusing on hands and being impervious to distracting words: «quelque chose qu’il dise pour distraire mon imagination, mes yeux ne quitteront pas ses mains...»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective misdirection combines persuasive verbal patter with high manual dexterity. If spectators concentrate solely on hands, the performer must increase technical proficiency; conversely, good patter can carry attention away from sleight-of-hand when appropriate for the audience.
